Article Title: Gulzar on Mumbai's influence: Gulzar reflects on Mumbai's influence on creativity; discusses the city's complex identity and cultural history
Article Text:
‘YEH SHAHAR MERA PARTNER HAI’

‘MUMBAI KA NAMAK ADAA KARNA PADTA HAI’

'For a translator, capturing the essence of his writing and his voice is very challenging'

'Gulzar saab doesn’t see the city only through rose-tinted glasses'





At the recently concluded literature festival at the NCPA, poet, lyricist and filmmaker Gulzar saab took the audience on a poetic journey through Mumbai, a city that has shaped his writing as much as he has chronicled its many moods. In a conversation titled Ek Shayar Iss Sheher Mein: A Poet’s Love Letter to His City, with translator Dr Rakhshanda Jalil and screenwriter-lyricist Kausar Munir as chair, Gulzar read from, 'Aamchi Mumbai: My City in Stories and Poems'. Written in Urdu and translated into English by Jalil, the book captures his enduring relationship with the city through its changing identity, people, seasons and the realities of migrant life. The session offered a Mumbai darshan through the words of a poet who has made the city an inseparable part of his creative journey.Explaining why he chose the word aamchi for the title, Gulzar traced it to Mumbai’s linguistic and cultural history, recalling the slogan that emerged during the debate over the capital of Maharashtra. “Bambai mein mushkil yeh hai ki aap kisi bhi zuban mein baat karein, aap bade conveniently reh letein hain. But I wish ke aisa na hota. Agar Bambai mein Marathi na bole aapka guzara na hota toh bada accha hota, kyonki fir aap badi jaldi Marathi seekh jaatein. Decades ago, when they were deciding what should be the capital of Maharashtra on the basis of language, there was a slogan: ‘Mumbai konachi?’ And the answer was: ‘Mumbai aamchi.’Aur maine 'Aamchi Mumbai wahan se chuna.”For Gulzar, however, the title is also deeply personal. The city is not merely the backdrop to his work but a collaborator that has influenced his stories, poetry and understanding of life. “Meri shayari, kahaniyaan, aur jo kuch maine yahan sikha, Babmbai ke saath hissa liya, yeh shahar mera partner hai. Yeh meri Mumbai lagti hai mujhe.”Reflecting on how Mumbai has influenced his writing, Gulzar spoke of growing and evolving alongside the city. Its atmosphere, he suggested, leaves a distinct flavour on those who live in it - one that finds its way into their work and their interactions with people. “I have learnt and changed with Mumbai. Iske saath saath hum sikhtein bhi rahein, badalte bhi rahein. Lekin Mumbai ka namak chakha hai yahan ki hawa mein, yahan ke samadar se udti hui jo aati hai. Uss namak ke hum kayal hain. Woah toh adaa karna padta hai. Agar namak chakh liya hai, toh aapki cheezein bhi namkeen ho jaati hain. Bahar bhi ghoomte hain toh log bhi namkeen lagte hain. Main uss namak ko kaise adaa karta, aur koi tarika nahi tha... I wanted to pay homage to this ‘namkeen’.”On the challenge of translating Gulzar Saab’s voice, at the 17th edition of Godrej Literature Live! The Mumbai LitFest 2026, Rakhshanda Jalil said, “Two distinct features of Gulzar Saab’s work are imagery and the way he talks through images and his voice. He has a childlike quality, a whimsicality of his own. For a translator, capturing this essence is very challenging. It is not just about craft or vocabulary. His voice is very distinctive. ”Talking about the city that emerges from Gulzar Saab’s writing, Kausar Munir said, "Socialism, realism, political consciousness, environmental concerns, all of this comes through in Gulzar Saab’s work. This new work isn’t just a romantic love letter to the city. There is a truth to it, there is a lived reality to it rather than a romanticised version of Mumbai. Gulzar saab doesn’t see the city only through rose-tinted glasses. ”
Article Summary: Aamchi Mumbai: My City in Stories and Poems is written in Urdu and translated into English by Dr Rakhshanda Jalil. The book captures Gulzar Saab's enduring relationship with the city through its changing identity, people, seasons and realities of migrant life.

Article Title: Minor’s parent fined Rs 15,000 over fake AI leopard photo
Article Text:
The department warned that using technology to spread false information about wildlife could invite legal action

Kolhapur

:





The forest department has fined the parent of a minor Rs 15,000 for circulating an AI-generated fake image of a leopard sighting in the Kalamba-Pachgaon area adjoining Kolhapur city, triggering panic among residents.On Friday, Oct 16, Sagar Dalvi, a Pachgaon gram panchayat member, alerted the forest department about a leopard allegedly spotted at Aptemala in Pachgaon. He also forwarded a photo he had received on his mobile phone. Forest officials and the wildlife rapid rescue team rushed to the spot but found no evidence of a leopard.Range Forest Officer Nandkumar Nalawade said an investigation revealed that a minor boy from Pachgaon had created the image using an AI app as a prank on his friends and circulated it on social media.“During investigation, it was revealed that a minor boy from the Pachgaon village had circulated the photo on social media. When our team questioned the boy, he lied about seeing a leopard out of fear. However, upon further questioning, he confessed that he had created a fake photo of the leopard with the help of an AI app to prank his friends and had made it viral. Later, the boy’s parents also admitted that this incident had happened unknowingly.A nuisance fine of Rs 15,000 was collected from the parent so that such thing won’t be repeated in future,” Nalawade said.The department warned that using technology to spread false information about wildlife could invite legal action.“Misusing technology to spread false news about wildlife behaviour in this way can lead to legal action. Citizens are appealed not to believe such rumours and not to forward any photos or messages without verifying them,” Nalawade added.The action was taken under the guidance of Deputy Conservator of Forests Dhairyasheel Patil and Assistant Conservator of Forests Priyanka Dalvi.
Article Summary: The forest department has fined the parent of a minor Rs 15,000 for circulating an AI-generated fake image of a leopard sighting. The image triggered panic among residents in the Kalamba-Pachgaon area adjoining Kolhapur city. The department warned that using technology to spread false information about wildlife could invite legal action.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Bengaluru artistes bring ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ to life at Dombivli Navratri festival
Article Text:
Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.





DOMBIVLI: A theatrical portrayal of Goddess Durga’s battle against demon Mahishasura offered Dombivli residents a glimpse into India’s traditional performing arts during the Sharadiya Navratri festival.Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale of the goddess’s victory to life.The programme was organised as part of the Navratri celebrations hosted by the Dr Shrikant Shinde Foundation and Shri Navdurga Yuva Mandal at the DNC school grounds in Dombivli East.Kalyan MP Dr Shrikant Shinde, who attended the event, stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional art forms that reflect India's cultural heritage.“Artistic performances that preserve our culture and traditions are important. They need encouragement and support so that this rich heritage can be passed on to future generations,” Shinde said.The presentation centred on the story of Mahishasura, whose tyranny threatened the world until Goddess Durga took the form of Mahishasuramardini to defeat him.Through a combination of theatrical expression, dance and devotional elements, the Bengaluru artistes depicted the goddess’s strength and the victory of righteousness over evil.Organisers said the festival seeks to go beyond religious rituals by providing a platform for India's diverse cultural and spiritual traditions. Alongside devotional activities, the programme features performances showcasing different forms of traditional art.At a time when modern entertainment platforms are increasingly popular, such performances offer an opportunity to introduce younger audiences to India's mythological stories and traditional artistic expressions.They also help preserve cultural practices that have been passed down through generations.The Navratri festival has included a range of religious and cultural programmes, including the Navkundatmak Sahasrachandi Mahayag, Haripath, bhajan sessions and devotional music.The organisers have sought to combine religious observances with cultural activities to give visitors a wider experience of the festival.The ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ presentation added a distinctive dimension to this year's celebrations, highlighting the role of traditional theatre in keeping India's mythological narratives and performing arts alive.
Article Summary: Bengaluru artistes presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil. The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale to life.

Article Title: Pune rail division organises Jan Samwad
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





Pune rail division organised Rail Jan Samvaad, an initiative which started a few days ago and is still underway, aimed at interacting with passengers to listen, understand and improve railways services and amenities through their concerns and suggestions, under a directive of Railway Board. Rajesh Kumar Verma , Divisional Railway Manager (DRM), Pune, led the programme at Pune railway station. Officers from Pune Division conducted the programme at major stations, while nominated officers and station managers organised the interactions at other stations.The feedback, suggestions and grievances received during the interactions were recorded and categorised into three levels for appropriate action. Short-term issues requiring immediate attention or quick resolution were addressed wherever possible, and necessary action was initiated on such suggestions. Medium-term issues requiring coordinated planning and implementation by the concerned departments were identified for further action. Long-term issues involving policy-level interventions, strategic planning or approval from higher authorities were documented for examination at the appropriate level.
Article Summary: Pune rail division organised Rail Jan Samvaad, an initiative which started a few days ago and is still underway. Officers from Pune Division conducted the programme at major stations, while nominated officers and station managers organised the interactions at other stations. Short-term issues requiring immediate attention or quick resolution were addressed wherever possible.

Article Title: Case against 4 for operating illegal dance bar under guise of live orchestra in Maval
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





Four people were booked by Pune Rural police for allegedly operating an illegal dance bar under the guise of a live orchestra in Sate village of Maval taluka.The case has been registered against the bar owner, an orchestra manager and two waiters under relevant sections of the Maharashtra Prohibition of Obscene Dance in Hotels, Restaurants and Bar Rooms and Protection of Dignity of Women (Working Therein) Act at Wadgaon Maval police station.Inspector Shankar Patil of Wadgaon Maval police received a tip-off on Friday night that around eight women were performing obscene dances on the stage of a live orchestra bar in Maval while patrons showered money on them. “Inspector Patil sent a team to the bar, but they did not find any women there, and the customers had started leaving the premises,” an officer from the Pune Rural police said.The officer said the police team then asked the bar owner to provide CCTV footage of the premises for the period between 9pm on Oct 22 and 12.30am on Oct 23. “The footage allegedly showed three women dancing in an obscene manner on a platform while customers watched them. It also showed a customer handing money to a waiter, who then showered it on the women.”
Article Summary: Four people booked by Pune Rural police for allegedly operating an illegal dance bar under the guise of a live orchestra. The case has been registered against the bar owner, an orchestra manager and two waiters under relevant sections of the Maharashtra Prohibition of Obscene Dance in Hotels, Restaurants and Bar Rooms.

Article Title: FTII alumna’s film on 12-year-old’s dream of becoming a doctor wins in Russia, Sweden
Article Text:
A still from Khilawadi (The One Who Plays), Shobhita Thakur’s award-winning film about a 12-year-old girl from Madhya Pradesh’s Banchhada community who dreams of becoming a doctor.

Pune:





Why should a girl’s future be determined by the caste she is born into? The question has remained with filmmaker Shobhita Thakur ever since she met girls from the Banchhada community in Madhya Pradesh.This Sept, when her 27-minute film Khilawadi (The One Who Plays), which follows the story of 12-year-old Sapna who dreams of becoming a doctor, won best short film at the Altyn Minbar Kazan International Film Festival in Russia, her beliefs were reinforced. In the Banchhada community where girls face pressure to enter sex work, that dream is an act of defiance.Thakur, an alumna of Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), said the issue had long been close to her heart. “I come from Madhya Pradesh, from a scheduled caste family of social activists. So conversations about social inequality were always part of our lives,” she said.The Banchhadas are a denotified community concentrated in Madhya Pradesh’s Neemuch, Mandsaur and Ratlam districts. Women and girls from the community have historically faced caste-based exploitation, including family-based sex work. Access to education and official documentation can also be difficult for families, particularly children whose fathers are not named on their records.“My father was a police officer. The difference between my life and these girls’ lives was stark. Had I been born into their families, or they been born into my family, things would have been very different,” she said. After graduating from FTII in 2012, she worked in advertising and corporate films, and as an executive at Netflix, before making this film.She spent two days in Neemuch getting to know girls and their families in the area. “We talked to the girls and listened to their stories. Some told me they could not get caste certificates because their fathers’ names were not available. For a small community that has little political visibility, even getting basic documentation can become a struggle because they are not considered a significant part of the vote bank,” she said.The film’s reception abroad has shown that the questions it raises extend beyond India. At a screening in Russia, one woman stood up and said the experience depicted in the film had happened to her. Audiences in Canada, Italy and France also responded to its themes.“We tend to think that people in first-world countries do not face these problems. That is not true. Women everywhere face restrictions on their agency, in different forms. The circumstances may differ, but the denial of their right to decide for themselves is universal,” Thakur said.Khilawadi has also won awards at Canada’s FascinAsian Film Festival and Pune’s Buddha International Film Festival, and received recognition at Sweden’s Sama International Film Festival. It has also been selected to be screened at the 45th Cambridge International Film Festival on Oct 26 and 30.For Thakur, the journey matters because Sapna’s story has travelled beyond the community in which it is rooted, prompting audiences elsewhere to confront questions of gender, caste and choice.
Article Summary: Khilawadi (The One Who Plays) follows the story of 12-year-old Sapna who dreams of becoming a doctor. The Banchhadas are a denotified community concentrated in Madhya Pradesh’s Neemuch, Mandsaur and Ratlam districts. Women and girls from the community have historically faced caste-based exploitation.

Article Title: Mankapur stadium turns into fortress for counting
Article Text:
Mankapur stadium

Nagpur:





With 110 CCTV cameras keeping watch and 84 counting tables being arranged, Mankapur Stadium is being transformed into a high-security centre ahead of Tuesday’s counting of votes for the Nagpur Division Graduates’ Constituency election.Unlike EVM-based elections, the manual counting of preferential ballots could stretch beyond 24 hours, with officials prepared to continue the exercise for up to 48 hours if required.A senior election official said preparations were nearly complete, with final arrangements underway at the stadium. “Of the 110 surveillance cameras installed, 32 are monitoring the strong room, while another 78 have been deployed in the counting rooms to ensure continuous surveillance throughout the exercise,” he added.Another senior official associated with the entire process said, “The strong room, where ballot papers from all six districts have been secured, was officially sealed at 6am on Saturday in the presence of the election observer, micro-observer and representatives of political parties,” adding that the sealing was carried out following the prescribed procedures to ensure transparency and security.A second round of training for officers involved in counting has also been scheduled at Mankapur Stadium on Monday to familiarise them with the procedures, particularly the complexities of preferential voting.Collectors from all six districts who are also the EROs, along with tehsildars, deputy collectors and other election officials, are expected to be present during the counting exercise.Officials said formal correspondence had been sent to govt of India and Election Commission of India , following which approval was received to conduct counting on October 27. The exercise will begin at 8am.The preferential voting system adds another layer of complexity. Officials must first identify valid ballots and determine the winning quota, calculated by dividing the total valid votes by two and adding one. If no candidate secures the required quota through first-preference votes, subsequent preferences will be examined according to the prescribed counting procedure.Officials said representatives of political parties would remain present during the entire exercise to ensure transparency at every stage.With 38 candidates contesting the election, including BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale and Congress’s Abhijit Wanjari, the administration is preparing for a potentially lengthy counting exercise.
Article Summary: Mankapur Stadium is being transformed into a high-security centre ahead of Tuesday’s counting of votes for the Nagpur Division Graduates’ Constituency election. Unlike EVM-based elections, the manual counting of preferential ballots could stretch beyond 24 hours. Officials prepared to continue the exercise for up to 48 hours if required.

Article Title: 38 boxes of liquor seized near Trimbakeshwar
Article Text:
Nashik

:





The State Excise Department’s ‘D’ Division in Nashik seized 38 boxes of Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) and beer worth a total of Rs 7.37 lakh, including the vehicle used to transport them, near Trimbakeshwar.Acting on a tip-off on Oct 23, a team from the Nashik unit set up a checkpoint on Harsul-Amboli Road at Vaghera Chaufuli under the Maharashtra Prohibition Act, 1949. During the inspection, officials stopped a hatchback and found 38 boxes of liquor and beer manufactured in Daman, Diu, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli, where their sale is permitted but their sale in Maharashtra is prohibited.The driver, Sumitkumar Patel (25), a resident of Valsad, Gujarat, was taken into custody. A case was registered against him and other suspected suppliers and purchasers under the Act.The raid was conducted by inspector N H Gosavi and his team under the guidance of senior state excise officials, including commissioner Rajesh Deshmukh, joint commissioner (Enforcement and Vigilance) Prasad Surve, divisional deputy commissioner Usha Verma, superintendent Santosh Zagade and deputy superintendent A S Tambare.On Oct 15, the Nashik State Excise Department had seized 16 boxes of liquor being transported in a hatchback at a checkpoint on the Trimbakeshwar-Jawhar Road near Amboli.The department has appealed to citizens to report illegal liquor manufacturing, sale and transportation. Information can be shared confidentially through its toll-free helpline at 18002339999, WhatsApp at 8422001133 or the office number 0253-2581033.
Article Summary: The State Excise Department’s ‘D’ Division in Nashik seized 38 boxes of Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) and beer worth a total of Rs 7.37 lakh, including the vehicle used to transport them. The driver, Sumitkumar Patel (25), a resident of Valsad, Gujarat, was taken into custody.

Article Title: TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards - UP Chapter to celebrate young changemakers in Lucknow on October 27
Article Text:
TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards - UP Chapter will honour outstanding achievers from Uttar Pradesh across multiple categories, including enterprise, sports, society, culture and social media.





TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards - UP Chapter will take place in Lucknow on October 27, bringing together achievers, emerging leaders and influential voices to celebrate young Indians shaping the country's future. The Awards will honour outstanding achievers from Uttar Pradesh across multiple categories, including enterprise, sports, society, culture and social media. The event will also feature discussions on UP’s transformation over the years, from improved job opportunities for youth to better safety and connectivity.At its heart, the summit will celebrate youth who are rewriting India's story through their ambition, ideas and achievements.The highlight of the event will be a special address by UP CM Yogi Adityanath, who will share his valuable insights on the state’s development initiatives, governance priorities and future vision. The CM’s address will also focus on the state’s efforts to drive growth, strengthen infrastructure and create new opportunities for the youth of Uttar Pradesh.Actor and parliamentarian Ravi Kishan will also deliver an address, sharing his perspectives on ambition, perseverance and the changing aspirations of India's youth.Para-badminton champion and IAS officer Suhas LY will share insights from his inspiring journey in sports and public service, marked by resilience and determination.Adding an entrepreneurial perspective to the programme, Aman Gupta, co-founder of boAt and Shark Tank India judge will lead a masterclass. The session will offer insights into entrepreneurship, brand building and navigating the challenges of turning an idea into a successful business.Former cricketer Mohammad Kaif will join a fireside chat titled ‘Small Town, Big Stage’, exploring his journey from Uttar Pradesh to the world stage. The conversation will reflect on the determination, opportunities and experiences that shape journeys from small-town beginnings to national and international recognition. Another fireside chat will bring the team of Hanuman Ansh together to discuss the film’s unprecedented success and what it takes to create content rooted in one’s culture.The event will also examine the state's changing identity through a panel discussion titled ‘UP Then and Now’, featuring actors Anupria Goenka, Faisal Malik and Dalip Tahil. The discussion will explore how Uttar Pradesh has evolved over the years, including shifts in its culture, aspirations and public perception. Another key session, ‘UP We Live In: Safety, Connectivity and Culture Through Young Eyes’, will focus on everyday experiences and expectations of young people. The panel ‘Degree to Destiny: Jobs, Skills and Startups in the New UP’ will explore how education, skill development and entrepreneurship are shaping career opportunities for the youth of Uttar Pradesh.Through conversations, masterclasses and recognition of exceptional achievers, TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards - UP Chapter aims to spotlight the people and ideas driving change in Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards - UP Chapter will take place in Lucknow on October 27. Awards will honour outstanding achievers from Uttar Pradesh across multiple categories, including enterprise, sports, society, culture and social media. Event will also feature discussions on UP’s transformation over the years, from improved job opportunities to better safety and connectivity.

Article Title: Chennai’s beloved ‘Damu Appa’ passes away at 72
Article Text:
Chef K Damodaran





K Damodaran, popularly known as Chef Damu, passed away on Sunday after a long illness. He was 72. He is best known for serving as a judge on the TV show ‘Cooku with Comali’, where he was fondly called ‘Damu Appa’ by participants.“He was one of my mentors, and one of the reasons for what I’ve become today,” recalls chef Koushik Shankar, widely known as Koushik, the mad chef. “Though he was a tough teacher in his younger days, he grew up to be an incredibly kind and helpful mentor for the younger generation. He also had a great sense of humour.”Chef Damu began his culinary career at the Taj Mahal Hotel, Mumbai, later working with Taj Chennai, ITDC and Sangam Hotels in Trichy and Madurai. Starting at the dishwashing station, his dedicationto the culinary arts earned him the Padma Shri in 2025. A cooking marathon where he prepared 617 dishes in 24 hours and 30 minutes, won him a place in the Guinness World Records “He was a wonderful person; respectful, cheerful and full of life,” said celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor. “I remember we were shooting for an advertisement once. Every time a shot was repeated, the crew would add more stains to our jackets to make it look authentic. Chef Damu and I would burst out laughing every single time.”While Chef Damu specialised in Chettinad dishes, seafood specialities and traditional vegetarian cuisine, he mastered several cuisines in his 50-year-long career, besides authoring nearly 30 books, says Koushik.However, his legacy lies not in culinary wisdom, but in the number of people he inspired to discover the joy of cooking, feels Rakesh Ragunathan, food historian. “Chef Damu was one of the pioneers who took the art of cooking beyond professional kitchens and into the living rooms of ordinary people. His work helped build a deeper connection between people and food, and he became a familiar and much-loved face in Tamil households. ”He made an immense contribution to bringing recognition and respect to the profession of chefs in India, says Sanjeev. “Chefs were not always given the respect they deserved. Even today, there is a need for more discussion about the profession and the people who work in it.”
Article Summary: K Damodaran, popularly known as Chef Damu, passed away on Sunday after a long illness. He is best known for serving as a judge on the TV show ‘Cooku with Comali’ His dedication to the culinary arts earned him the Padma Shri in 2025.

Article Title: Elephant trapped in slush at Gunderipallam dam near Erode; rescue operations under way
Article Text:
Photo by S Parthiban





ERODE: A female elephant got trapped in slush at the Gunderipallam dam near Gobichettipalayam in Erode district, prompting a major rescue operation by forest and fire service personnel on Sunday.Wild animals have been frequently entering the dam vicinity in search of drinking water due to acute water scarcity in the forest. The water level in the Gunderipallam dam, located in the T N Palayam forest range, has dropped in recent weeks. In the early hours of Sunday, a female elephant that came to the dam to drink water got stuck in the slush in the exposed portion of the reservoir. “Unable to free itself, the animal struggled for several hours and was trumpeting in distress,” said a forest officer from the T N Palayam forest range.On being alerted by residents, officials and staff from the T N Palayam forest range and personnel from fire and rescue services rushed to the spot and launched rescue efforts.As the elephant had become exhausted after being trapped in the slush for several hours, teams began efforts to pull it out using ropes and an earthmover. However, the rescue operation suffered a setback when an earthmover deployed for the task got stuck in the muddy terrain.The incident delayed rescue operations.Forest authorities made alternative arrangements by bringing in another earthmover to rescue the elephant. A veterinary team from Sathyamangalam has been mobilised to provide medical assistance and monitor the elephant’s condition.
Article Summary: Wild animals have been frequently entering the dam vicinity in search of drinking water due to acute water scarcity in the forest. The water level in the Gunderipallam dam, located in the T N Palayam forest range, has dropped in recent weeks.
